messages:
mina: Hey team — hitting a persistent auth-retry when using `redwoodctl login --sso` while running the sample app. After completing the browser/device flow the CLI shows success but the sample app immediately logs 401 and the CLI re-prompts the device flow in a loop. mac + linux repro.

rahul: yikes. quick Qs: which CLI version and how are you running the sample app (env vars)?

mina: `redwoodctl 1.4.3` (homebrew). repro: in one tab `REDWOOD_PROFILE=sample node sample-app/index.js` (app calls embeddings via local SDK). in another tab run `redwoodctl login --sso` -> browser auth completes -> CLI prints success. but sample app prints `auth: token refresh failed (401)` and `redwoodctl whoami` shows not logged in.

mina: I inspected `~/.config/redwood/config.json` — the device flow wrote the token under profile `default` only; my `sample` profile was untouched. local SDK is reading REDWOOD_PROFILE=sample so it sees no token and triggers login.

rahul: sounds like device flow is ignoring explicit REDWOOD_PROFILE/env precedence and always writing to default on first-run. two fixes: make login respect REDWOOD_PROFILE and `--profile`, and change write logic to merge with existing profiles instead of replacing.

ellis: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/cli/issues/1622 (sso: device flow writes to default, breaks non-default profiles). short-term workaround: run `redwoodctl login --profile sample` or `export REDWOOD_PROFILE=default` before login.

devex-bot: added labels: sso, auth-loop, devex. Suggestion: add a small note to sample-app README about `--profile` to avoid confusion during onboarding.

mina: thanks — workaround works. please add the README note, saved me a few minutes.
